text:
Linda: FYI — ACME reported a sudden spike in 95th/99th latency for embedding requests in eu-central after last night's infra glidepath rollout. CS opened a ticket.
Ravi: on it. can you paste a sample trace or request id from CS?
CS_Escalations: Ticket #2347. Example request_id=acme-req-20260707-89ab. 95th jumped from ~120ms to ~1.4s, 99th ~2.6s. Error rate unchanged. No auth failures.
Santiago: timeline — we rolled CUDA runtime 12.2.1 -> 12.3.0 and applied GPU microcode patch at 01:45 UTC. Also kernel backport for blk-mq qdisc at 02:30. Might be related.
Linda: customer timeline matches. They saw the jump start at ~02:50 UTC.
Ravi: quick check — is NVMe qdepth saturated on the hosts serving their shards? grabbing iostat and iostat -x output now.
oncall-bot: [alert] host eu-c-23: nvme_io_avg_qdepth=24.8 (threshold 20) — flagged at 02:52 UTC.
Santiago: that qdepth is high. Could be IO interference from KV cache flushes after kernel change. Any flush heartbeats around that time?
Ravi: logs show periodic kvcache flush every 5m starting 02:48, prolonged flush durations (~900ms) after the kernel backport. Cropped log:

```
[02:48:12] kvcache: flush start shard=acme-1 size=24GB
[02:48:13] storage: nvme write latency avg=850ms p95=1.2s
[02:49:00] kvcache: flush end duration=48s
```

Linda: so flushes holding up storage IO, pushing up tail latency for small embedding write/read paths — that matches p95/p99 behaviour.
CS_Escalations: Customer notes that only embedding endpoints were affected (small, frequent requests). Generation routes fine.
Santiago: hypothesis: kernel backport changed blk-mq scheduling or IO merge behavior -> long flush I/O bursts -> GPU threads waiting on host IO for KV eviction -> token path latency spike for embeddings.
Ravi: repro attempt on a repro host (eu-repro-07) using same kernel + cuda + microcode. I can reproduce ~1.3s p95 for embedding calls when flush is triggered.
Linda: good repro. what's a quick mitigation for ACME while we fix infra?
Santiago: options:
- Temporarily route their embedding traffic to dedicated nodes in eu-c-15 (older kernel) — quick and safe.
- Throttle kvcache flushes (increase watermark / backoff) on affected hosts.
- Rollback kernel backport on a small subset.
Ravi: routing would be fastest. I can add a route rule to send ACME's tenant ID to eu-c-15 for 30m while we triage.
CS_Escalations: customer prefers a reroute if it won't break consistency. They're on non-sharded config so routing is fine.
Linda: Ravi, do it. Also take a snapshot of nvme SMART + dmesg for the hosts.
Ravi: doing route now. curl to control-plane API I used:
```
POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/route_rules
{ "tenant": "acme", "route_to": "eu-c-15", "ttl": 1800 }
```
Response: 200 OK — rule applied. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: [notice] routing rule applied for tenant=acme -> eu-c-15 at 03:05:12 UTC.
CS_Escalations: customer confirmed latency dropped to baseline within 2m. :relieved:
Santiago: next steps for infra team: collect vmstat, iostat -x, blk-mq counters, and kernel perf memstall traces during a flush. Also check NVMe firmware version differences.
Ravi: captured iostat and dmesg and uploaded to /internal/incidents/7077777000/ — filenames: iostat_eu-c-23.log, dmesg_eu-c-23.log, kvflush_trace.log
Linda: temporary rollback plan if routing isn't acceptable: roll kernel back on a canary host and run canary load test against embeddings.
Santiago: also look at adaptive kvcache thresholds — we may tune to avoid big synchronous flushes when host IO busy.
CS_Escalations: customer asked for ETA. We told them mitigation in place and will follow up with root cause and a permanent fix within 48h.
Ravi: will coordinate with infra on rollback or kernel patch. tagging eng-infra for triage. @Santiago can you own the RCA? :pray:
Santiago: I'll own it. First pass: compare blk-mq scheduling traces pre/post backport and NVMe firmware behavior under large sequential writes. Also see if the CUDA microcode patch changed any DMA patterns.
Linda: thanks. I'll update the ticket and include reproducer steps for support.
CS_Escalations: Reproducer for eng:
1) On repro host with kernel K and CUDA 12.3.0 run a background kvcache flush of 20GB.
2) Run embedding load: curl -X POST https://api.redwood/run_embeddings -d '{"tenant":"acme","model":"embed-lite","inputs":[...]}'
3) Observe 95th/99th latency jump.
Code example:
```
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do 
  curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
   -d '{"inputs":["q"]}' https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings | jq -r '.latency_ms'
done
```
Santiago: good. I'll push logs and a short write-up to the incident folder and propose kernel patch revert if blk-mq change is root cause.
Ravi: once we have RCA, schedule a controlled rollback or kernel upstream fix. Also assess longer-term: move small/frequent embedding traffic to dedicated NVMe lanes or add per-tenant IO shaping.
Linda: agreed. Closing loop: routing mitigation worked, customer satisfied for now. Tracking ticket lifecycle — RCA owner: Santiago. Follow-up due in 48h.
oncall-bot: [update] incident 7077777000 set to status=mitigated, owner=Santiago, sla=48h.
